structured.approach: I read the two contracted inputs. feat.tasks shows the Data Science lane has TSK-03 and TSK-04, both in ap_forecast. org.engineering_stack gives the stack, the CI command and the branch rules. The hook for this step allows no shell commands, so I didn't run git. Instead I checked the brief's tool view and read the repository files directly: .git/HEAD, .git/config, the reflogs for dev and feature/story, __init__.py, ci.py, predict.py and explain.py. From these I confirmed the repository is available, the branches and base commit are as expected, write access is in place, the upstream isn't set yet, and the code the two tasks will build on. I then wrote task.repo_access with three open questions, none of them blocking. I didn't use any connector because the inputs had everything this step needed.

claims.text: The Data Science lane's tasks TSK-03 (STORY-03) and TSK-04 (STORY-04) both target the ap_forecast repository; no new repository is needed.
Repository ap_forecast is available locally, the working tree is clean and the agent identity has write access.
Branch feature/story is checked out and was created at commit d67e866; dev was created from origin/dev at d67e866.
The remote origin is https://github.com/arghya05/ap-forecast-sample.git; main and dev track origin, and feature/story has no upstream configured yet.
No Databricks, database or other workspace is used by ap_forecast.
CI is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py and enforces coverage >= 90 (COVERAGE_MIN = 90.0), no print/eval/exec, no bare except and lines at most 140 characters.
The current ap_forecast version is 0.9.0 and TSK-03 owns the version step.
predict_delay_days(history) and build_explanation_request(vendor, predicted_days, config=None) exist today, which TSK-03 and TSK-04 build on.
ci.py imports the third-party coverage package.

open_questions: RAQ-1: feat.tasks names branches feature/<story>, but the branch created is literally feature/story. Should TSK-03 (STORY-03) and TSK-04 (STORY-04) share it or get per-story branches? Interim: both tasks on feature/story, each commit prefixed with its story ID.

RAQ-2: ci.py needs the third-party coverage package. This step allowed no shell commands, so I couldn't check whether it is installed for /usr/bin/python3. Interim: assume it is; the first CI run will confirm.
RAQ-3: Push permission to origin wasn't tested because only the spine pushes. Write access is taken from tool:repo-access.
structured.summary: ap_forecast is ready for the Data Science work (TSK-03 and TSK-04) on FEAT-ZD-48600. It's the only repository the lane needs, so nothing has to be created. The branch feature/story is checked out at d67e866, the working tree is clean, the agent identity has write access, and no Databricks or database is involved. I wrote task.repo_access.md with the repository baseline (version 0.9.0, the CI bar, and the existing functions the tasks extend) and three open questions, none of them blocking: whether both stories share one branch, whether the coverage package is installed, and that remote push permission couldn't be tested.
